name: Judeo-Moroccan Arabic

ancestors.notes: Judeo-Arabic macrolanguage node (ISO 639 jrb): a sociolinguistic/orthographic collective, not genetic descent (see jrb.json notes) -- aju's single genetic PARENT is ar-MA, matching the engine constraint that every language has at most one PARENT ancestor.
Regional descent: Judeo-Moroccan Arabic is fundamentally a variety of Moroccan Darija, historically written in Hebrew script.
Hebrew liturgical/lexical adstrate, shared with the rest of the Judeo-Arabic continuum (jrb.json).

notes:
STUB. Judeo-Moroccan Arabic (ISO 639-3 aju), the variety or varieties of Moroccan Darija spoken by Moroccan Jews, historically written in Hebrew script (also called Judeo-Darija / El Haketía in some regions, though Haketía proper is the more Spanish-influenced Judeo-Arabic of northern Morocco). Wikipedia (Judeo-Moroccan Arabic) notes distinctive features such as س /s/ pronounced as /ʃ/ and ز /z/ as /ʒ/, a layer of Hebrew lexical borrowings, and in some regions Hispanic features from Sephardi migration after 1492. These are real, citable phonological tendencies, but a complete letter-to-IPA grapheme table requires deciding the specific Hebrew-script orthographic conventions used for Judeo-Moroccan texts, which was not sourced with confidence this session (no JIPA illustration or dedicated phonology paper was fetched). graphemes intentionally empty pending that sourcing pass, per the 'never fabricate' rule.

RESOLVES TO ITS PARENT'S TABLE, WHICH IS A PLACEHOLDER. This spec declared a parent and no `graphemes_base`, so it produced no phonology at all and the code resolved to an empty table — a caller asking for it got nothing, silently. It now inherits, so the code reaches a usable table. That table is the parent's and is NOT a claim about this variety: no reflex here has been checked against a source. `quality` stays `stub` for exactly that reason. Replace the inherited table with cited reflexes before treating any reading here as this variety's. The parent it already named, ar-MA, is the one it now inherits from.
